Create new *_map_seq() functions

Source: R/function-map-seq.R
function_map_seq.Rd

function_map_seq() creates a sequence mapper from a basic mapper such as grim_map(): a function that varies the reported values a few steps up and down and tests each resulting value set, as grim_map_seq() does. By default, only inconsistent value sets are dispersed.

See vignette("consistency-tests-in-depth"), section Sequence mapper.

function_map_seq() is a developer tool: it may change in a minor release, with a NEWS entry.

Usage

function_map_seq(
  .fn,
  .var = .reported,
  .reported,
  .name_test,
  .name_key_result = "consistency",
  .name_class = NULL,
  .args_disabled = NULL,
  .dispersion = 1:5,
  .out_min = "auto",
  .out_max = "auto",
  .var_bounds = NULL,
  .include_reported = FALSE,
  .include_consistent = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

.fn

A basic mapper function such as grim_map(), typically made by function_map(). It must return its input data frame with a logical column named by .name_key_result added.

.var

String. The variables that the factory-made function disperses by default. Defaults to .reported.

.reported

String. All variables the factory-made function can disperse.

.name_test

String (length 1). Plain-text name of the test, such as "GRIM", for messages and the output's class.

.name_key_result

(Experimental) String (length 1). Name of the key result column. Default is "consistency". Must be the value that .fn was created with.

.name_class

String. Optionally, one or more classes to add to the output. Default is NULL.

.args_disabled

String. Optionally, names of arguments of .fn that the factory-made function should reject.

.dispersion

Numeric. Steps up and down from the reported values, in units of the last decimal place. Default is 1:5.

.out_min, .out_max

Limits on the dispersed values. A number applies to every dispersed variable, and NULL removes the limit. Default is "auto", which takes the limit from .var_bounds.

.var_bounds

Named list, or NULL (the default). Each element is named after a variable in .reported and is a numeric vector of its least and greatest possible value, with NA for an unbounded side, such as list(n = c(1, NA), sd = c(0, NA)). A variable not named here is unbounded, except for n, which always has a minimum of 1. For a bound that depends on a setting, an element may also be a function that takes the settings .fn recorded for its call, as a named list such as list(sd_meaning = "sd_sample"), and returns such a vector. The bounds only keep impossible values, such as a sample size of 0, from being tested. They have no bearing on consistency.

.include_reported

Logical. Should the reported values themselves be part of the sequences? Default is FALSE.

.include_consistent

Logical. Should consistent value sets be dispersed as well? Default is FALSE.

...

These dots must be empty.

Value

A function such as these:

Factory-made functionDispersed variablesTest vignette
grim_map_seq()"x", "n"vignette("grim-in-depth")
grimmer_map_seq()"x", "sd", "n"vignette("grimmer-in-depth")
debit_map_seq()"x", "sd", "n"vignette("debit")

The settings of .fn, i.e., its arguments after ..., such as rounding, are arguments of this function as well, with the same defaults. So are its helper arguments, such as items_averaged. Its ... pass any other arguments on to .fn, which is only of use for a .fn without ... of its own.

Details

The arguments of function_map_seq() set the defaults of the corresponding arguments of the factory-made function, which can be overridden in each call.

Each variable in var is dispersed around its own reported value while the others stay as reported.

To export a factory-made function from another package, follow the purrr FAQ on adverbs; see vignette("consistency-tests-in-depth"), section Context and export.

Conventions

Name the factory-made function after .fn with _seq appended, as in grim_map_seq() from grim_map(). The output has the classes "scrutiny_map_seq" and "scrutiny_{tolower(.name_test)}_map_seq". Prefix any class you add via .name_class with your package's name, as in "mypkg_schlim_map_seq".

Examples

# Function definition of `grim_map_seq()`:
grim_map_seq <- function_map_seq(
  .fn = grim_map,
  .reported = c("x", "n"),
  .name_test = "GRIM"
)
